ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Theory before vs after test — must understand generation effect confound
ground_truth.original_snippet: Participants were asked to write their theory after the test phase was completed.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Participants were asked to write their theory before the test phase was completed.
ground_truth.description: Changed theory-writing from after to before test — act of generating theory could inflate understanding scores in Theory condition (generation effect), confounding the understanding measure

matched_finding.subcategory: treatment confounds transmission with theory generation and test priming
matched_finding.description: The "Configurations + Theory" condition changes several things at once: participants receive a theory, are told they will write a theory, and actually write one before the understanding test is completed. Any treatment difference could therefore reflect articulation, reflection, metacognitive prompting, or test priming rather than transmission per se. This prevents clean causal attribution to inherited theories.
matched_finding.quote: in which participants could also formulate an explicit written theory about the physical system and transmit it to the next participant in the chain. ... Participants were asked to write their theory before the test phase was completed.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Absolute estimation vs comparative judgment — must know these tap different constructs
ground_truth.original_snippet: Participants’ understanding was evaluated by presenting them with pairs of wheels that differed in their configurations, and asking them to predict which wheel would reach the bottom of the rails first.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Participants’ understanding was evaluated by presenting them with pairs of wheels that differed in their configurations, and asking them to estimate how long each wheel would take to reach the bottom of the rails.
ground_truth.description: Changed from comparative judgment (which wheel first) to absolute estimation (how long) — measures different construct; absolute timing requires calibrated knowledge, not relative understanding

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: All-previous vs last-two configurations — must understand information parity in transmission chain designs
ground_truth.original_snippet: Participants could consult their two last configurations between any trials.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Participants could consult all of their previous configurations between any trials.
ground_truth.description: Changed from last-two to all-previous configurations — breaks information parity with between-generation transmission, confounding cumulative cultural learning with individual data accumulation

The robustness of the model estimates was checked by running additional models (see below). Additional models with more efficient sampling confirmed the reported res...
ground_truth.description: Deleted MCMC convergence warning AND robustness checks — hides computational problems with primary model and the verification that alternative specifications confirmed results

matched_finding.description: The stated reason for abandoning the preregistered model is not convincing. A negative correlation between two outcome components does not inherently justify collapsing them; it suggests the need for a different model specification, such as multivariate, separate binomial, or hierarchical models with correlated random effects. Replacing the preregistered analysis with an aggregated-score analysis changes the estimand and weakens confirmatory inference.
matched_finding.quote: However, analyses revealed that understanding scores about inertia and centre of mass were negatively correlated (Supplementary Figure 9 and Supplementary Table 7) and some individuals better understood inertia than centre of mass while others better understood centre of mass than inertia (Figure 3I and Supplementary Figure 2). As a result, the preregistered model did not converge so we ran our analysis on aggregated score

matched_finding.subcategory: results are inconsistent with claimed absence of understanding
matched_finding.description: Elsewhere the manuscript acknowledges that participants were above chance and had useful intuitions about the system. This is inconsistent with framing the study as showing improvement in the absence of causal understanding. The results are more compatible with partial, biased, or dimension-specific understanding than with no meaningful understanding at all.
matched_finding.quote: Participants who did not inherit any theory (“Configurations” treatment) scored similarly (and better than chance) on questions about inertia and questions about centre of mass (Figure 3I). ... This indicates that participants had appropriate intuitions about how to maximize acceleration

matched_finding.description: The confirmatory analysis was not purely preregistered: the final model was selected by comparing candidate models based on fit to the observed data. This introduces researcher degrees of freedom and undermines the inferential strength of the preregistration, especially when used to support strong confirmatory claims.
